findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) in Webhook Dispatcher
findings.description: The webhook registration endpoint allows unauthenticated callers to specify arbitrary destination URLs, permitting internal network pivoting to cloud metadata and private microservices.

evidence.request:
POST /api/v2/webhooks/subscribe HTTP/1.1
Host: api.payments.enterprise.internal
Content-Type: application/json

{"callback_url": "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/"}

aiTriage.businessImpact: Unauthenticated attackers can query cloud metadata service (IMDSv1) and pivot to internal payment databases.
aiTriage.exploitabilityAssessment: Directly exploitable without prior authentication via public webhook subscription endpoint.
aiTriage.reasoning: Scanner evidence confirmed IAM credential reflection in response body.

findings.title: Unauthenticated Redis Cache Exposed on Internal Subnet
findings.description: Internal Redis cluster instance lacks authentication requirement (requirepass disabled), allowing arbitrary read and write of session tokens and payment nonce caches.

evidence.rawOutput:
INFO Server
redis_version: 7.0.11
role: master
keyspace: db0:keys=14205,expires=8920

aiTriage.businessImpact: Complete compromise of active session keys and merchant authentication tokens stored in volatile cache.
aiTriage.exploitabilityAssessment: Exploitable once perimeter access or internal network pivot (e.g. via SSRF) is established.
aiTriage.reasoning: Direct response to INFO command returned full cluster status without AUTH challenge.

findings.title: SQL Injection in Settlement Reconciliation Query
findings.description: The settlement batch reconciliation endpoint constructs raw SQL queries via string concatenation, allowing extraction of full cardholder ledger tables.

aiTriage.businessImpact: Direct exfiltration and modification of production payment ledgers and customer transaction records.
aiTriage.exploitabilityAssessment: Confirmed SQL injection with schema extraction payload execution.
aiTriage.reasoning: Database metadata was reflected in response object confirming successful injection.

findings.title: Overly Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)
findings.description: API returns Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * alongside Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, enabling cross-site data theft from logged-in browser sessions.

aiTriage.businessImpact: Authenticated user session data can be scraped by malicious third-party websites visited by employees.
aiTriage.exploitabilityAssessment: Requires user interaction (phishing link or malicious origin visit).
aiTriage.reasoning: Wildcard/reflected origin with credentials verified by header response inspection.

findings.title: Hardcoded Weak JWT Signing Secret in Service Configuration
findings.description: The internal microservice authentication module uses a static hardcoded HMAC key ("payments_secret_key_2024!"), permitting arbitrary token forgery.

evidence.payload: Static string literal detected in codebase

aiTriage.businessImpact: Attacker who knows the hardcoded secret can mint administrative JWTs with elevated authorization claims.
aiTriage.exploitabilityAssessment: Trivial token generation once the static secret is known or decompiled.
aiTriage.reasoning: Hardcoded fallback value discovered in production build code path.

aiTriage.businessImpact: Potential security vulnerability requiring standard defensive hardening.

attackPaths.title: Public SSRF → Internal Redis Compromise → Ledger SQLi Extraction
attackPaths.summary: An unauthenticated attacker exploits SSRF on the public webhook API to reach the unauthenticated Redis cache, acquires internal service credentials, and pivots to the settlement ledger database via SQL injection.

scoreBreakdown.explanation: Formula: Exposure (24/25) + Exploitability (24/25) + Asset Criticality (25/25) + Chain Multiplier (21/25) = 94/100.

prerequisites: Flat internal subnet routing between API and Redis cluster
attackPaths.impactAssessment: Total compromise of cardholder transaction history, bank routing numbers, and payment audit logs.
recommendedFixSequence: Implement strict URL whitelist validation and block internal RFC1918 & metadata IPs on WebhookService (Neutralizes Stage 1)
Enable Redis requirepass authentication and restrict Redis subnet ingress (Neutralizes Stage 2)
Convert LedgerRepository raw SQL concatenation to parameterized PreparedStatements (Neutralizes Stage 3)

attackPaths.title: Hardcoded JWT Secret → Admin Token Forgery → Microservice Takeover
attackPaths.summary: An attacker leveraging code leaks or decompiled binaries utilizes the hardcoded HMAC secret to forge administrative JWTs, bypassing API authorization checks.

scoreBreakdown.explanation: Formula: Exposure (18/25) + Exploitability (23/25) + Asset Criticality (22/25) + Chain Multiplier (19/25) = 82/100.

prerequisites: Knowledge of hardcoded JWT fallback string
attackPaths.impactAssessment: Unauthorized generation of valid administrative tokens for all internal payment microservices.
recommendedFixSequence: Rotate signing keys and enforce mandatory KMS / Vault secret injection at runtime
Remove fallback strings from codebase and add CI SAST blocking rule

attackPaths.title: Perimeter Ingress SSRF Pivot to Internal Redis Cache & Token Interception
attackPaths.summary: An adversary triggers the SSRF on /api/preview to query internal cloud metadata and pivot into unauthenticated api.example.test.
prerequisites: Direct HTTP connectivity to public gateway API
attackPaths.impactAssessment: Exposure of cloud access credentials and lateral movement into the private compute tier.

scoreBreakdown.explanation: Deterministic Contextual Formula: Exposure (25/25) + Exploitability (22/25) + Asset Criticality (25/25) + Chain Pivot Impact (18/25) = 90/100.

recommendedFixSequence: Patch SSRF at /api/preview with strict URL schema and domain whitelisting
Enable password authentication and ACL on api.example.test

attackPaths.title: SQL Injection in Financial Ledger to Complete Database Takeover
attackPaths.summary: Exploitation of unsanitized parameters at /api/accounts enables arbitrary SQL execution against the PostgreSQL production cluster.
prerequisites: Valid application session or API query capability
attackPaths.impactAssessment: Direct exfiltration and modification of financial transaction records.

scoreBreakdown.explanation: Deterministic Contextual Formula: Exposure (25/25) + Exploitability (25/25) + Asset Criticality (25/25) + Chain Pivot Impact (18/25) + Unauth Crown-Jewel Modifier (+5) = 98/100.

recommendedFixSequence: Convert dynamic SQL queries at /api/accounts to parameterized prepared statements
